subject: nobs as a function of two init iteration variables?

messages.author: cf427545797c4df8
messages.subject: nobs as a function of two init iteration variables?
parts:
Good afternoon,

I'm attempting to use the handy createModels() function to write a series of input files for a simulation that I'm working on.  The nobs depends on two of the variables I iterate over in the init section: nclusters and clustersize, as the nobs = nclusters*clustersize (balanced clusters).

However, I haven't figured out how to specify this via the syntax.  The few things I've tried end up with errors.

Failed example 1:
[[init]]
...
nclusters = 100 30 20;
clustersize = 20 30;
...
[[/init]]
...
montecarlo:
nobs = [[nclusters]]*[[clustersize]];
...

results in nobs = 100*20; (which makes sense, after I think about it)

Failed example 2:
I defined the nobs via the DEFINE command:

define:
numberoo = [[nclusters]]*[[clustersize]];

montecarlo = numberoo;

This results in an error message because the argument (numberoo) is not an integer.

Any suggestions / thoughts / ideas?  I've looked through the vignette and the solution hasn't yet occurred to me.

Thanks in advance,
Chris Runyon
PhD Student, Quantitative Methods, UT Austin

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] nobs as a function of two init iteration variables?
parts:
Hi Chris,

At the moment, we don’t plan to implement products of iterators in the template language, but you should be able to use the mplusModeler facility (esp. the updated one on Github) to achieve this sort of thing using more typical R syntax. Here’s a bit of starter code:

library(MplusAutomation)

beta <- 1:4
gamma <- 1:4

m <- mplusObject(MONTECARLO="NAMES ARE Y X; NOBS=100; NREP=5;",
    MODEL="Y ON X M; M ON X;",
TITLE="Model with multiplied coeffs")

for (b in beta) {
  for (g in gamma) {
    thism <- m 
    thism$MODELPOPULATION <- paste0("Y ON X*", b, " M*", b*g, ";")
    out <- mplusModeler(thism, modelout="mc.inp", run=1L)
  }
}

Best,
Michael
